Current text-based dialogue systems excel at generating text that sounds human-like, but they fail to grasp the underlying structure of actual human conversations, limiting their practical applications. We introduce the LEATHER model, which learns and utilizes a structured framework to engage in text-based dialogues naturally. Designed to model both natural and lexicogrammatical structures, the model combines multiple representations and uses them both to create more authentic dialogues and ask targeted, structured questions. We demonstrate the LEATHER model's practicality by showing its ability to adapt its language based on the language of its interlocutor and achieve better performance in dialogue-based tasks compared other systems by 2.4 points on the dataset it was developed on. Furthermore, the model can extract and utilize structured information, allowing it to ask structured questions even when interacting with humans, and outperform existing state-of-the-art systems significantly.

This talk will examine lattice Qcd under conditions of non-zero temperature and density, discussing how these simulations are conducted and presenting findings from my own research on the properties of nuclear matter under these circumstances.

A widely used approach in the renewable energy industry involves calculating 10-minute mean wind speeds from readily available data, albeit at a high computational cost, making it unsuitable for large-scale probabilistic assessments. To overcome this limitation, researchers have developed an efficient alternative based on regression kriging that predicts mean wind speeds over large areas, and can be easily applied to multiple locations. Once computed once, the algorithm allows for instantaneous retrieval of sampled time series. To further refine accuracy, a neural network-based proxy model has been developed using regression kriging data, and can accurately replicate observed wind speeds. To account for model uncertainty, the proxy model incorporates Gaussian process variance, allowing it to represent both the model's confidence and system uncertainty. To validate the accuracy of the algorithm, it was tested using data collected from ten offshore wind turbines, and the results showed minimal model error.

Twitter has become a valuable tool in social media analysis, allowing real-time tracking of social interactions through data mining. Natural disasters, in particular, can be effectively monitored by analyzing Twitter posts, providing insight into public sentiment. By examining the impact of the 7.2 magnitude Izmir earthquake in Turkey on 30 January 2020, researchers identified distinct trends in Ishan's post-quake behavior compared to those of others.

A group exhibiting the $R_\infty$ property when considered with reduced cohomology systems having values in $\mathbb{Z}_2$ is referred to as a $R_\infty$ group for such systems. Groups that are universally nilpotent in this context can be identified by a particular polynomial degree, specifically the degree $d$ nilpotent groups show the $R_\infty$ property starting from $\text{cd}_{R_\infty}(G) \le 2d - 1$. We investigate the $R_\infty$ characteristic in generalized solvable Baumslag-Solitar groups and their nilpotent quotients.

A data-driven approach, integrating a physics-based model and experimental data via an optimization technique, enables accurate predictions even when key model parameters are unknown. This method, utilizing trajectory data, is highly effective for modeling complex molecular dynamics. It is analogous to machine learning's supervised model, but with an added benefit of incorporating physical model consistency. Notably, this approach, known as trajectory inversion, has been applied to optimize molecular structures and fluid dynamics, and is a versatile and efficient method for predictive modeling. This method's internal nature allows it to be easily adapted to incorporate additional information, such as gradient-enhanced models, and demonstrates superior performance compared to standard model-based approaches. Notably, this method excels in achieving generalization with minimal data requirements.

Naturalistic Driving Datasets enable researchers to examine real-world driving behavior.  A novel neural-driven dataset, SceNDD, is presented in this research, which combines scene-driven events and 3D point cloud data.  This new dataset is based on real-world driving scenarios captured using point cloud sensors.  An automated event detection system was developed to identify and segment different events.  The events were also annotated by hand to provide a more comprehensive view.  Both automatic and manual annotations were used to verify the reliability of different detection methods.  Additionally, the Scene-driven Naturalistic Driving Dataset (SceNDD) was made publicly available to facilitate research on scene-driven events using 3D point cloud data.

In one-dimensional spatial dimensions, a newly introduced concept called reflected entropy has gained prominence in the fields of quantum information theory and the conformal field theory in dimensional space. This concept can be mathematically expressed as the length of a specific geodesic within a specific bulk region known as the RT surface. The dimension-independent nature of reflected entropy in spatial dimensions led us to explore its application in various boundary/conformal field theories in finite temperatures, across all spatial dimensions. This case study focuses on a specific boundary/conformal field theory known as the BCFT${}_{1+2}$ theory. By analyzing this theory, we aim to derive a general formula for the reflected entropy of a specific region and explore its implications for entanglement phase transitions. Furthermore, we examine this phenomenon in the context of the entanglement structure of composite systems composed of BCFT${}_{1+D}$ theories.

The integration of the intelligent and dynamic metasurface, known as a RIS, has emerged as a crucial component in future communication systems. The employment of RIS in the reception end of the transmitter can significantly enhance the communication performance. Nonetheless, the performance of RIS-assisted OFDM systems is compromised by the presence of hardware impairments and the resulting loss of orthogonality. In this paper, a novel RIS-assisted OFDM system, utilizing an enhanced Extreme Learning Machine, is proposed to mitigate the effects of these impairments. The system is designed to operate without the need for a conventional channel estimation process by training the ELM with simulated data. The proposed system is evaluated by comparing its error rate and bit error rate with that of a conventional OFDM system, demonstrating its effectiveness in combating hardware impairments and channel noise.

This work examines how systems evolve over time, specifically looking at their energy changes, based on the system's current state. A new statistical method is developed to measure this for specific system states. The results show that systems experiencing rapid changes follow a particular mathematical rule regarding these changes. To test this, the study looks at a simple system of two interconnected systems that exchange particles and changes in this setup support the finding that this mathematical rule can be verified.

We examine the deformation theory of G2-instantons on a nearly G2-manifold. When the nearly G2-structure arises from a 2-form exact under a Killing vector field. This leads to a one-parameter family of metrics, causing the nearly G2-structure to evolve into a genuinely nearly G2-structure. Under a specific condition met by Salamon metrics, we derive a formula for the first-order deformation of an instanton under such a change, and subsequently identify conditions for the existence of a one-parameter family of G2-instantons.

The global COVID-19 pandemic has spurred the creation of contact tracking apps, with NCA's being developed by governments to assist in containing the spread of the virus. These apps track individual movements to facilitate infection control, with some governments adopting mass testing and tracing strategies. To prevent data breaches, NCA developers must prioritize data encryption. This study investigates the confidentiality of Portugal's NCA, Coronav\'irus-SUS, by examining its code and associated documentation. We discovered that location and address history, as well as personal contact information, collected by Coronav\'irus-SUS are stored unencrypted, posing a significant risk of data compromise.

Recently, there has been significant interest in combining quantum computing and neural networks into a unified algorithm. Initially, neural networks were employed as a means to decode quantum information. In contrast, when used in an information-rich setting, these networks struggle to learn from certain quantum states, known as entangled states. Interestingly, when the quantum data dimension is very large, even simple quantum circuits can learn from such states more efficiently than their neural network counterparts. In a comparable framework, researchers found that the performance of these algorithms could be compared to classical machine learning methods. Notably, when dealing with highly entangled states, the performance of these algorithms could be predicted based on properties such as area laws and von Neumann entropies, which are commonly used in quantum computing and neural networks. In addition, while neural networks have limitations, their ability to introduce randomness and use dropout, a method to enhance performance in various algorithms, could help them overcome this issue and potentially compete with other algorithms in certain situations.

Recently, there has been a significant increase in interest in software proof assistants and their ability to verify complex computer programs with intricate syntax and semantics. This interest is driven by the practical need for more sophisticated proof assistants. This paper describes an experimental tool that enables programmers to write complex C code utilizing features like pointers, data structures, and standard C libraries, as well as utilize an embedded scripting language based on S-exprs to simplify the process. This tool, which is built on top of the ACL2 theorem prover, combines the expressiveness of C with the ability to generate C code and proofs automatically.

A comprehensive study of the 39910 Iochroma group asteroids' dynamics has been conducted, focusing on the long-term effects of resonances and planet interactions over 450 Myr timeframes, utilizing numerical integrations via the REBOL code. Iochroma group members, characterized by low inclinations and unknown compositions, are restricted to a small area within 400-405 in semi-major axis. Iochroma group dynamics are significantly influenced by the 3:5 mean motion resonance with Jupiter as well as other shorter and longer resonances with Jupiter. Furthermore, encounters with other planets in the group play a role in shaping its dynamics. Iochroma group dynamics are diverse, with some subclusters emerging due to the influence of the 3:5 resonance, while others are dispersed due to encounters with other planets over a relatively short timescale.

Building upon the classic Euler-Zagier multiple zeta function and the Hurwitz Zeta function, a novel double zeta function is introduced, which generalizes and converges for all positive integer parameters. Ramanujan's theorem on single zeta values is then extended to more complex scenarios, which involve mixed zeta values and Dirichlet L-functions at odd prime locations. These results, in many instances, replicate the style of supertrivial identities exemplified by Ramanujan's findings, and numerous examples of the type of identity he discovered are provided.

We establish that the logical circle-equivariant elliptic cohomology of the quotient space $\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}(V)$ is equal to the direct sum of circle-equivariant cohomology groups $H^\ast_\mathbb{C}(V^{\mathbb{C}}; \ell_\mathbb{C})$ over all even weight spaces $V^{\mathbb{C}}$, where $\mathbb{C}$ denotes the complex numbers and $\ell_\mathbb{C}$ is an elliptic line bundle over a specific elliptic curve $E$. This finding has significant implications in the study of elliptic cohomology of unitary Grassmannians and projective spaces.

We've developed a novel approach inspired by algebraic topodynamics to tackle physical problems, specifically focusing on calculating the Tamm-Dancoff approximation in light-matter correlations using machine learning. We've created a dataset of problems with known solutions by generating random topological structures, then employed machine learning models to learn the connections between homology groups and the Tamm-Dancoff approximation. We've successfully tested the model on real-world quantum systems and obtained results that are as accurate as traditional approximation methods, but with significantly reduced computational effort, ultimately revealing the model's limitations in certain new physical contexts.

This research focuses on the next-to-leading-order analysis of the $J/\psi$'s angular distribution in the $e^{+}e^{-} \to J/\psi +\eta_c,\chi_{cJ}$ reactions. To carry out the study, we have developed a computational tool for this process. We have then determined the relevant cross-sections, which are presented in terms of the $J/\psi$'s helicity. Furthermore, we have analyzed the $M1$- and $B1$-type contributions to the $J/\psi+\eta_c$ reaction, in addition to the $M1$- and $B1$-type transitions to the $J/\psi+\chi_{c0}$ reaction. We have also investigated the $M1$- and $B1$-type transitions to the $J/\psi+\chi_{c1}$ and $J/\psi+\chi_{c2}$ reactions to examine the $M1$ and $B1$ amplitudes. We have then calculated the $J/\psi$'s production rate in the $e^{+}e^{-} \to J/\psi$ reaction at the BESIII and Belle II experiments, which reveals that the $M1$ and $B1$ transitions are strongly suppressed.

This research aims to enhance the design of Signal PINs by examining how users employ them.
Similar studies on other systems have identified the primary functions of passwords.
The findings of this study suggest that the main purpose of Signal PINs is security.
To gather more insight, we conducted a survey among Signal users.
The results indicated that approximately 70% of the users could articulate the purpose of Signal's encryption policy, yet only about 30% could explain how the PIN contributes to this process.
The findings also reveal that the majority of the users utilize PINs with four or more characters.
The data further shows that the majority of the users employ Signal on the Android platform and set their PINs within the range of four to six characters.
The study also reveals that the majority of the users set their Signal PINs after receiving the first suspicious activity alert.
The findings also demonstrate that the majority of the users set their Signal PINs after receiving the first suspicious activity alert.

To efficiently integrate solar energy produced by photovoltaic panels, researchers have developed Gaussian quadrature methods that can calculate average solar energy with high precision. While some implementations of Gaussian quadrature exist, they often lack the necessary precision for modern data sets. A new solar-weighted Gaussian quadrature rule has been proposed and tested to calculate average solar energy more accurately. By analyzing its theoretical properties and testing it on real solar energy data, the new method demonstrates excellent performance in calculating average solar energy and energy produced during consecutive hours.

The curvature entry point theorems have significantly impacted non-smooth analysis, optimization, and variational problems, with initial proof methodologies rooted in geometric analysis and complex analytical techniques being difficult to apply in practical scenarios like machine learning optimization. Our new approach, the curvature entry point theorem via the generalized Gauss-Newton model, provides a structured, two-step foundation that translates non-smooth objectives into manageable forms through the Gauss-Newton approximation and subsequent application of probabilistic subspace theory techniques, thereby enabling the use of well-established low-dimensional optimization methods.

This paper examines the impact of grammatical gender on representations of nouns in three languages (Finnish, German, and Russian) that utilize gender-based gender-marking. We create a dataset for identifying grammatical gender in these languages and investigate the impact of gender-related features on the representation of nouns in each language. We also compare the representation of gender-neutral nouns (mostly feminine) with their male counterparts using our constructed dataset. Our analysis shows that while end-to-end neural models for gender-assignment can identify gender-related cues with high accuracy, manually engineered features are still more reliable. Additionally, removing content from the training corpus for gender-assignment results in the loss of gender-related information from the models, resulting in lower accuracy. Finally, our study reveals that feminine nouns are more likely to have male counterparts, which we believe could be a consequence of women's underrepresentation in society.

This work focuses on the properties of certain types of arithmetic groups, which are defined as irreducible lattices in Lie groups of a specific algebraic structure, derived from a number field, under a specific signature condition. These groups are shown to be non-characteristic-trivial and hence charmonic. The proof involves the use of a Riemannian geometry argument, which establishes that these groups are rigid when considering their Cayley complexes, under certain conditions. Additionally, the paper explores the concept of quasi-isometric rigidity of these groups as well.

We introduce an innovative neural network-based approach for object position estimation, capable of detecting objects categorized as novel, unseen during training. The proposed method leverages image-level data from the training set, along with zero-shot category embeddings, to enable object position estimation. Building on the success of Deep Image Pyramids, we utilize their output as a basis for position estimation, incorporating fully convolutional networks to translate the features into pixel-level segmentation masks. The architecture's convolutional nature allows us to incorporate batch normalization and residual connections, enhancing our capability to handle an extensive number of novel classes. Experimental results demonstrate that our Position Estimation with Image Pyramids and Convolutional Networks model achieves superior accuracy on challenging benchmarks, including the NYUv2 and Sun RGB-D datasets, when compared to prominent counterparts, such as SemSeg, SegNet, and UNet.

Traffic forecasting is a crucial aspect for optimizing urban transportation systems, yet existing methods struggle with the vast size and sparseness of traffic data. To address these limitations, a new approach leveraging extensive and sparse traffic information has been developed. This method automatically extracts meaningful attributes based on neighborhood similarities between different regions, enabling the integration of both local and global traffic patterns. The combination of these derived attributes significantly enhances the accuracy of forecasted results compared to traditional methods when applied to sparse traffic datasets.

This study introduces a family of Variational Graph Autoencoders, a dependency learning model based on probability distributions, capable of extracting and representing latent variables from observed data. The model not only learns the structure of dependencies between visible and hidden variables, but also allows for capturing alternative realities by incorporating interventions and imagining alternative scenarios. Theoretical proofs demonstrate the model's ability to accurately learn structural causal models and accurately reconstruct data distributions. Through simulations, the model outperforms traditional probabilistic learning models in tasks that require understanding and manipulating underlying causal relationships.

Radio astronomy, specifically the capture of millisecond transients, is a critical component of the facility's activities.  Irish LOFAR has incorporated REALTA, an automated system designed to detect and record radio transients in real-time.  Following a brief introduction to REALTA, the initial results from its operations demonstrate successful data collection of various types of radio transients.  A key feature of REALTA is its ability to efficiently sort and manage large volumes of captured data, ultimately yielding a refined list of truly unique and novel radio transients.  Upon filtering, the system identified six potential new radio transients within the surveyed area, further highlighting REALTA's capabilities.

Recent advancements in machine learning and artificial intelligence have led to
innovations in metaphotonics, enabling enhanced chip-based photonic devices and
circuits through optimized material arrangements. To address complex
multidimensional optimization issues, algorithms such as genetic algorithms and
particle swarm optimization have been employed to fine-tune algorithms for the
improvement of chemical compositions, architectural designs, waveguide patterns,
and pixel layouts. Additionally, machine learning has facilitated faster light
modulation, signal processing, and light-matter interaction capabilities. This
research aims to showcase the metaphotonics field's remarkable potential for
technological innovation, leading to groundbreaking photonic applications.

The film industry has long been a rich source of artistic expression and a complex marketplace driven by both creative and business considerations. Understanding the connection between a film's narrative and its commercial appeal is a significant area of inquiry, yet existing knowledge is hindered by the lack of a comprehensive, detailed dataset that accurately captures the range of film content. This study fills this gap by compiling a extensive database of over 10,000 films, each with over 20,000 recorded details, including content descriptors, making it possible to explore the influence of a film's content on its popularity. Furthermore, to address the limitation of a common dataset that only includes 2,500 films, our dataset enables a more thorough examination of the relationship between a film's predicted popularity and its actual box office earnings. This study reveals that a film's genre and other key features significantly impact its commercial potential, with the most profitable films often being comedies, dramas, and action films. Notably, films with award-winning directors, producers, or high-budget productions have a higher likelihood of commercial success. Interestingly, while a film's genre has a substantial effect on its popularity, films with similar genres can exhibit significant variations in commercial success. This study also explores the predictive accuracy of a regression model on test datasets, revealing that while the model is reasonably accurate, it is not a perfect fit.

This research aims to examine the stabilization of voltage under auxiliary frequency regulation in power systems, which prioritizes frequency stability over auxiliary frequency regulation hierarchy. The paper's findings are based on two key assumptions: auxiliary frequency regulation uses a significantly higher gain than primary frequency regulation, and the system experiences small disturbances. The study employs a Lyapunov function to demonstrate that the closed-loop system's state converges exponentially to a desirable equilibrium point, which coincides with the nominal state when auxiliary frequency regulation has an infinitely large gain. The research includes two crucial comparisons: how auxiliary frequency regulation affects voltage stability compared to no frequency regulation at all, and how its effectiveness is influenced by network parameters, disturbance magnitudes, and system operating conditions. The paper's conclusions are validated through numerical case studies.

The integration of cyber systems with physical systems has produced numerous innovative applications, ranging from the control of industrial machinery to sophisticated medical devices. As technology advances, systems capable of autonomous decision-making are being developed, paving the way for complex networks of cyber-physical systems (CPS) that exhibit cognitive capabilities. These networks will surpass traditional systems in capabilities, but will also introduce complex and unprecedented challenges, including system design, security, and maintenance. In this context, the paper outlines the characteristics of future cyber-physics systems, explores the key challenges they will face, and discusses potential solutions, ultimately highlighting the need for research focused on enabling CPS to operate harmoniously within societal frameworks.

A newly developed method, partially polarized inverse external Compton, allows for the calculation of coherent Com scattering effects on polarized light from astrophysical sources, including astrophysical plasmas. By combining this approach with a Monte Carlo technique and a polarization matrix, researchers can model and analyze the polarization properties of polarized light from these sources, including a specific excess in UV and soft X-ray wavelengths. A comparison between theoretical and observational data revealed that blazar spectra exhibit this excess, which is more pronounced with the use of Monte Carlo simulations than with inverse external Compton models based on optical or radio emission. Furthermore, the polarization of this excess is predicted to be relatively high, ranging between 10-30%.

Recent advances in image processing technology have driven significant 
improvements in digital image analysis techniques. Building upon these 
techniques, an algorithm has been developed that facilitates image matching 
over complex landscapes, such as areas with dense vegetation, by providing a 
method to field-verify satellite images. Following image matching, an analytic 
function is created using corresponding feature points extracted from both 
images to facilitate precise location conversion between them. Furthermore, 
the algorithm incorporates numerical optimization methods, including BFGS and 
Broyden, as well as a new approach called Diagonalized Adaptive Memory 
Poisson (DAMPo), to optimize feature point correspondence. Experimental 
results indicate that the DAMPo method achieves superior performance in 
approximately 60% of tested cases, compared to traditional BFGS and Broyden 
algorithms.

This research focuses on developing optimal strategies for identifying pure states with specific symmetries. We propose "virtual detection," which involves identifying an unknown state |ψ⟩ by measuring projectors associated with symmetric subspace |ψ̃⟩ and its orthogonal complement. We found that if |ψ⟩ has a non-zero overlap with |ψ̃⟩, then virtual detection is feasible and we determined the best projective measurement strategy to achieve this. We also found conditions for when a state |ψ⟩ cannot be distinguished using virtual detection and developed a method to verify these conditions. Additionally, we showed that if |ψ⟩ is not detectable, then a better strategy exists, which does not rely on projectors for |ψ̃⟩ and its complement.

Baryon-antibaryon pairs are generated through the splintering of a quantized, helically coiled QCD string. The paired baryon and antibaryon are formed when the splintered portions of the string detach and hadronize. The model explains the observed patterns in baryon-hadron cross-section ratios, particularly in their dependence on spin and orbital states.

The 22-year magnetic cycle exhibits its longest current patterns running from the northern to southern hemispheres, a phenomenon known as the "magnetic-cycle parity." Researchers have proposed that the electric currents present during this cycle could impact the detection of north-south travel time by sound waves. To investigate this, a numerical magnetic field was designed to replicate solar active areas, and a mathematical approach was used to calculate the additional sound wave deflection caused by magnetic currents. The study found that these currents can produce disturbances in active regions up to 3000 km in diameter, but do not contribute significantly to global correlations. The implications of these findings on helioseismic diagnostics of magnetic fields are also discussed.

Gravitational waves can have a significant impact on the magnetic fields of galaxy clusters, 
which typically have strong magnetic fields.  Fluctuations in these fields produce strain 
patterns similar to those caused by the LIGO band, and can be represented by a random 
stochastic process.  The characteristics of this pattern can be measured using the 
autocorrelation function and power spectral density.  Observations made with the VLA have 
revealed that such magnetic field fluctuations can be linked to the characteristics seen in the 
Pulsar Timing Spectrum band, and can potentially be used to constrain the redshifted power 
spectrum.  By combining redshift information with a model of magnetic field evolution, 
it's possible to establish limits on the energy density and spectral index of gravitational 
waves, within specific intervals, without being constrained by the LIGO upper limits.

Light field technology has garnered significant attention in the imaging field due to its capacity to provide multiple views simultaneously, enabling various downstream applications. This work involves collecting data from multiple angles and processing it to optimize compression, disentanglement, and light synthesis capabilities. Current state-of-the-art methods treat each view within each subset identically, disregarding the inherent variations in image content across different viewpoints. This paper proposes an approach that acknowledges the underlying spatial redundancy present in light field images by employing two neural networks, one for predicting redundant information and another for predicting unique components. This proposed model outperforms existing techniques in achieving ultra-low distortion while requiring a modest increase in computational resources.

Cross-language information retrieval is a crucial component of multilingual information processing systems. Current studies aim to develop cross-lingual space mapping techniques, but achieving effective space alignment remains a challenge. We introduce two innovative approaches within cross-lingual information retrieval frameworks, namely a statistical vector-based interactive model and a deep neural network-based noninteractive model. Evaluations demonstrate the semantic improvement of retrieved vectors through clustering, as well as the deep model's capacity to effectively capture cross-lingual space mapping and achieve high performance in retrieval and ranking, surpassing current state-of-the-art results.

Accurate health and demographic data are crucial for informed policy decisions and resource allocation. However, data are often collected in large areas, which can be problematic for nations with irregular administrative divisions and limited resources. In such cases, there is a pressing need for methods that can make precise estimates within smaller regions. This paper delves into two model-based approaches to make design-based estimates available in smaller areas, focusing on the context of low and medium-income countries. Specifically, it examines the pooled regression model and the Bayesian hierarchical model that incorporates the predictive information from the design-based model. Although the Bayesian model offers a direct link to the design-based estimate, it may not always outperform the latter in terms of mean squared error. In contrast, the pooled regression model provides this link but may not always yield better results. Ultimately, this paper recommends adopting the pooled regression model for policy recommendations and further research into Bayesian models for their potential supplementary role in design-based estimation.

This study explores the use of quantum systems in a game of chance. The use of quantum strategies can lead to winning rates that surpass those possible in classical strategies. When specific conditions are met with certain systems, these strategies can guarantee a 100% win rate. However, when these optimal conditions are not met, there are still opportunities to increase the probability of winning. It's also explored how this scenario changes when players can use an unlimited supply of quantum resources.

This study is a combined theoretical analysis of the two-dimensional compounds consisting of four elements in the formula MA$_2$Z$_4$. We used density functional theory to calculate the structural properties and an empirical pseudopotential method to predict the electronic band structure and optical behavior, adjusting for the inherent limitations of density functional theory through the use of hybrid functionals. We also performed density functional theory+U calculations to correct the underestimation of transition metal d states in the hybrid functional calculations and found that despite variations in energy levels, the four-component compounds exhibit consistent band alignment. We further investigated the interaction between adjacent layers, identifying the unique stacking-independent exciton located between the valence band maximum and conduction band minimum, and confirmed that it exists regardless of the specific arrangement of the four-layer structure.

The first instance of a Cabibbo-suppressed decay, specifically $\Sigma^+ \to p \mu^+ \mu^-$, has been observed in the decay of $B^0$ mesons. This phenomenon involves both lepton-contact and radiative transitions, primarily driven by neutral current Higgs and $Z$-penguin loop effects. Our study employs the factorization approach along with light-front Regge theory to model these transitions, resulting in model predictions for the $B^0$ decay into $B^0$ and $\Sigma^+$ particles as well as the $\Sigma^+ \to p \mu^+ \mu^-$ decay itself. This prediction can be tested by the LHCb experiment.

A comprehensive, observation-driven model of planet formation is developed by simulating the physical processes involved in the formation of a protoplanetary disk through the rupture of a cold, dense nucleus. By combining these processes with recent findings from the field, a realistic timeline of planet formation is created. A protoplanetary disk forms by merging with the surrounding envelope, and its mass is regulated by the balance of gravitational forces and the disk's ability to support itself. Over time, a photoevaporation wind develops, removing excess envelope material and leaving behind the disk. This process can occur at different stages of disk evolution, and its effects are more pronounced in younger disks. In addition, small-scale instabilities and the formation of gravitationally-bound clumps are simulated, and these processes can lead to the birth of planets. Finally, the model explains how planetary systems evolve and how planets interact with their surroundings, and it explores the implications of this process for the observed properties of exoplanets.

When observing the sky from ground, we are affected by two types of scattering processes: Rayleigh and Mie scattering. To accurately simulate what we see, we need to develop a model for the atmosphere that takes into account both processes and is based on the specific conditions at the time of observation. A proper model allows us to predict the atmospheric color and consistency of our measurements, which is essential for space-based instruments to be calibrated. In this research, we present a detailed study of the factors influencing atmospheric scattering and provide a comprehensive model that can be used by astronomers to interpret their observations. We found that atmospheric humidity and dust are important contributors to the atmospheric scattering, especially during sunrise and sunset. Our model, which incorporates measurements of Rayleigh and Mie scattering, allows us to predict the atmospheric color with high accuracy. We also found that humidity and dust can have a significant impact on the atmospheric color, which means that their effects need to be carefully considered when interpreting astronomical observations. Overall, our research provides a valuable tool for astronomers to understand the unique conditions of atmospheric scattering and to interpret their observations with greater accuracy.

In the field of recurrent neural networks, the inherent sparsity of sequential data can be leveraged to enhance modeling efficiency. By focusing on the inherent structure of temporal sequences, researchers have developed multi-term recurrent neural networks. However, traditional sequential recurrent neural networks often neglect this structure. In this paper, we introduce the multi-term temporal sparse recurrent neural network, which efficiently models temporal sparsity while maintaining local connectivity. Furthermore, we extend the concept to the multi-term temporal sparse Bayesian recurrent neural network, incorporating the process of variational inference. By relaxing the sequential recurrence, the training speed of the model is significantly improved, and a speedup of 5-10 times is achieved on the ATIS dataset.

One way of formulating Grigoriev's (2009) result is that a group of homeomorphisms on the interval from 0 to 1 cannot be embedded into a group of continuous endomorphisms on the same interval. This statement can be rephrased by drawing an analogy to Pontryagin duality for abelian groups. Under Pontryagin duality, a group of continuous group endomorphisms on the interval from 0 to 1 corresponds to a specific type of discrete group known as the profinite completion of the integers, denoted as the restricted direct product of Z/|n| for n in the natural numbers. Since the profinite completion of the natural numbers is homeomorphic to the interval from 0 to 1, this creates a self-dual correspondence. This self-duality implies that groups of continuous homeomorphisms on the interval from 0 to 1 cannot be embedded into groups that facilitate continuous reasoning, which in the context of this analogy, is represented by the group of continuous endomorphisms on the interval from 0 to 1. This inability to embed groups of continuous homeomorphisms into groups that facilitate continuous reasoning stems from the fact that groups of continuous homeomorphisms on the interval from 0 to 1 are not discrete. This limitation highlights a fundamental challenge in the development of discrete probabilistic groups of continuous transformations. This issue was further explored by the author in the context

In scenarios where data privacy is of utmost importance, machine learning models are trained using a distributed approach in which local datasets remain on separate devices. Local models are adjusted independently and only summary information is sent to a central server, which aggregates the models into a global version. However, the model predictions may still be subject to fairness issues, which can potentially be exploited to infer sensitive data characteristics. 

This paper highlights a federated learning attack that leverages the disparity between the local and global models to infer the fairness of the training data, and an alternative method for inferring data sources based solely on model outputs. 

A proposed "blending" technique is introduced, which integrates the global model and local predictions to enhance data source identification difficulty and mitigate fairness biases within the federated learning environment. 

In addition, the paper discusses a variant of federated learning known as Vertical Federated Learning, which involves merging datasets from different sources and may expose participants to fairness challenges based on their specific data categories. 

A proposed solution, known as Differential Confidentiality, utilizes cryptographic keys and public information to establish a shared framework for training, thereby circumventing fairness biases in FWL and enhancing secure communication.

A theoretical framework combining supersymmetry and a extra $U(1)_X$ gauge symmetry is suggested. This framework includes right-handed neutrinos that can have dark matter and dark energy properties. Specifically, the dark energy is attributed to a right-handed neutrino's mass, which is a linear combination of three $U(1)_{B-L}$ and two $U(1)_{X_L}$ gauge couplings. This model can also resolve the matter-antimatter asymmetry in the universe through right-handed neutrino interactions. Additionally, this model can be tested using the LHC, which can probe $Z'$ interactions and supersymmetry, as well as neutrino oscillation experiments.

In recent years, intelligent reflecting surfaces have garnered significant attention in wireless communication due to their potential to optimize energy efficiency. However, as an emerging technology, practical implementation is hindered by the need for accurate channel estimation. To address this challenge, a low-power wireless powering system is incorporated to obtain channel information, but the resulting channel updates are slow and impede data transmission. To mitigate this issue, a novel method is proposed to partition the smart surface into multiple segments, utilizing a dedicated transmitter to power these sections simultaneously. This multi-segment surface is then paired with a deep learning-based detection method to enhance performance while maintaining low power consumption. A specific type of neural network is designed to process binary channel update information, and a novel, unsupervised learning method is developed to effectively train this network in the absence of labeled data. Simulation results demonstrate a significant improvement in the network's maximum achievable throughput, along with a substantial reduction in the computational complexity of the network.

For the first time, researchers investigated the large two-neutron isomer in the $^{186}$Hg nucleus to explore its properties and decay characteristics. The study involved a detailed examination of the $^{186}$Hg nucleus's energy state, specifically its excited state at 313 keV, located above the proton drip line. The investigation utilized a data set collected at the ISOLDE facility, employing a $\beta$-$\gamma$ coincidence method, and focused on transitions following the $^{186}$Hg nucleus's large two-neutron isomer at an energy of 247 keV. The study confirmed the 247 keV isomer's significant 313 keV excited state, characterized by a $\beta$-decay transition to the ground state of $^{186}$Au, demonstrating a 13.7 ns half-life. The research also identified the $^{186}$Hg nucleus's large two-neutron isomer's $\beta$-decay characteristics and found they were consistent with theoretical predictions. The study's results significantly expanded the known $\beta$-decay properties of the $^{186}$Hg nucleus.

Our analysis is based on a detailed framework combining the Standard Model and a unified SO(10) gauge theory, along with fermions in the 16 representation and right-handed neutrino singlets. This setup enables the dark matter candidate, the lightest stable odd-grade fermion, and the right-handed neutrino to generate the dark matter density, repulsive force, and baryogenesis through the leptogenesis process, respectively. By comparing the dark matter density, matter-antimatter imbalance, and various lepton process rates with available data, our study yields constraints on the model's parameters. Notably, the matter-antimatter imbalance is effectively managed by lepton process rates. Moreover, our research demonstrates that the dark matter density can be accurately predicted using the matter-antimatter imbalance and the mass of the dark matter fermion.

Machine learning has recently demonstrated remarkable success in solving complex control problems, particularly for robotic locomotion, thanks to the development of deep reinforcement learning. However, an inherent drawback of deep reinforcement learning is its reliance on extensive trial-and-error in an interactive setting. To mitigate this, researchers have proposed leveraging demonstrations or expert knowledge, yet the effectiveness of these approaches is often constrained by the availability of demonstration data. This paper presents a novel data-driven control method, suitable for dynamic locomotion tasks, that efficiently utilizes and integrates various types of limited demonstration data, such as IITs and expert knowledge. The proposed approach combines information from multiple sources to construct a unified state-value function, optimizing policy and control parameters simultaneously. Experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of this unified data-driven control method in achieving complex locomotion tasks, including advanced maneuvers like achieving and traveling, backflips, backflips and takeoffs, and backflips and takeoffs and takeoffs, utilizing diverse data sources with as few as 50 trials.

Ward relations are derived for the conformal quantum theory rooted in the Beilinson--Lebedev realization of the Gaudin model, specifically for the $\mathfrak{sl}_3$ Toda theory. Furthermore, we establish the impact of the Virasoro algebra on the Beilinson--Lebedev representation and develop the L operator's action on the Virasoro descendent of the Beilinson--Lebedev vacuum.

Image GANs excel at disentangling real from fake images, yet their ability to learn complex relationships within image content remains limited. As a result, their generated content often falls short in conveying nuanced relational aspects. To address this gap, we introduce the Relation GAN, a model that focuses on connecting related content, with its generator taking paired pairs of real and fake images as input, with the goal of replicating the characteristics of their real counterparts. To achieve effective relational learning, we devise the triplet loss, an objective function that guides the generator to preserve structural relationships from the real domain in the generated domain, with FID serving as a metric for the quality of the emulation. Notably, our proposed model is capable of learning multiple structures within source images, with our relational GAN approach outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods in multiple applications, including grayscale-to-color, image restoration, and color transfer tasks.

A potential solution to the distance limitations of quantum key distribution is the twin-field QKD method, notably in its CTK method which achieves key rates comparable to repeater-based methods while requiring less strict conditions on phase synchronization than earlier TFQKD protocols. Although CTK method can operate without precise phase synchronization in the asymptotic limit, it necessitates precise synchronization in finite-key scenarios; this paper introduces a revised protocol with even lower requirements on phase synchronization accuracy while maintaining distance-independent key rates, and provides an analysis demonstrating the reduced phase synchronization requirements in the absence of any eavesdropper.

This paper delves into the Toeplitz algebras $\mathcal{T}_\mathfrak{D}$ on Numerical Range free domains $\mathfrak{D}$, particularly those with at least besselian and semi-Bergman characteristics. We define $\mathcal{T}_\mathfrak{D}$ as the $C^*$-algebra generated by a family of Bergman projection operators $P_{\mathfrak{D}}$ on a Bergman space $\mathcal{H}(\mathbb{B}_n)$. We find that $\mathcal{T}_\mathfrak{D}$ is isomorphic to $\mathcal{T}_\mathbb{D}$, the Toeplitz algebra associated with the unit ball $\mathbb{D}_n$, and explore its ideal structure. We identify specific maximal ideals within $\mathcal{T}_\mathfrak{D}$, and prove that $\mathcal{T}_\mathfrak{D}$ possesses the BFN property. We also demonstrate that $\mathcal{T}_\mathfrak{D}$ is approximately divisible and provide the inductive limit description of its quotient $C^*$-algebra $\mathcal{T}_\mathfrak{D}/\mathcal{K}$.

This research presents a method for real-time identification of objects mentioned in phrases within video content, such as "detect every book present in this room". Unlike traditional object detection systems that rely on predefined sets of objects and produce bounding boxes with high computational costs, our approach leverages an extensive database of object categories and a visual assistant to continuously propose potential objects based on the content of the phrase. To improve efficiency, our system only considers suggestions that fall within the visual frame of reference of the phrase, as indicated by annotations made by a human operator. By leveraging a deep learning model that can accurately predict bounding boxes, our approach minimizes the need for high-computation tasks while maintaining a high level of flexibility in terms of object categories and phrase structures. Furthermore, our proposed annotation technique simplifies the training process by only requiring pseudo bounding boxes of objects that are correctly identified, as opposed to a full annotation of a video dataset. Through thorough evaluations conducted on two video datasets, our system has demonstrated its effectiveness and adaptability, outperforming state-of-the-art object detection systems and significantly reducing the required computation time.

The Rho Ophiuchi molecular cloud is one of the most studied regions in the Orion complex, where the S1 region is actively forming stars. Previous studies have shown that the density of the region is primarily controlled by the radiation from the T Tauri star TMC-1CX, with the exception of the area surrounding the Herbig Ae/Be star S1, where its optical depth has been observed to be less than 1.5. In this study, we used the ALMA and VLT/ESPA to observe the radiation from the region surrounding S1 at different wavelengths and found that the area is densely populated. In particular, the area is primarily composed of three distinct regions: an ionized region, an atomic region, and a photodissociation region. By analyzing the data from ALMA and VLT/ESPA, we found that the radiation from the region is primarily controlled by the radiation from the T Tauri star TMC-1CX, with the exception of the area surrounding S1, where a new source of radiation has been discovered. This area is primarily composed of an ionized region, where the radiation from the source is primarily controlled by the radiation from the T Tauri star TMC-1CX, and by the radiation from the source, where the radiation from the source is primarily controlled by the radiation from the T Tauri star TMC-1CX.

Transformer architectures, initially developed for natural language processing tasks, have recently garnered significant attention in computer vision applications. Contrasting with the traditional CNN approach, the transformer architecture employs a self-attention mechanism that facilitates the seamless integration of spatially dispersed image components. This review aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the contemporary state of transformer-based methods in vision tasks, focusing on three main areas: adapting existing transformer architecture for vision, revisiting attention mechanisms, and integrating the best aspects of both CNN and transformer approaches. Furthermore, this review will highlight relevant benchmark datasets and offer insights into the strengths and limitations of transformer models in vision, ultimately guiding future research directions.

Mortality data from 1900 to 2019, including data from 10 countries, are analyzed to understand whether using a model with fewer components is better than another with variable component loads. We examine the LASSO's ability to select relevant components and compare the two models, one with variable loads and the other with fixed loads. Our aim is to determine which model is most effective at predicting future mortality.

This research investigates the cause of neural architecture exploration instability and proposes solutions to mitigate it. The instability issue is analyzed in depth, and an indicator of disruption is identified. Two effective approaches for disrupting prevention are proposed: employing regularization techniques and selecting candidates based on diverse metrics. Notably, when combined with the MultiScale NAS algorithm for benchmark image classification tasks, these prevention strategies demonstrate significant improvements in model accuracy and efficiency.

This research introduces an innovative attribute abstraction framework for analyzing and representing time series data, which can enhance the predictive accuracy and interpretability of machine learning models. An applied demonstration of this approach is provided, which utilizes various feature extraction methods within the R-based theft, a package that has been open sourced. The demonstration showcases how to perform attribute sampling, identify characteristics, and make model-based predictions based on distinct time series datasets. Furthermore, the demonstration covers evaluation methods and an inherent visualization tool designed to inspect the extracted attributes within the theft package.

Building upon the concept of intrinsic convexity developed by Cartan and Busemann, we examine the intrinsic convexity properties of a metric space known as a 'environment', which arises from its subspace's completion. It's proven that geodesically complete, intrinsic convex CAT(0) environments cannot include bounded, open convex subsets with infinite intrinsic convexity diameter. Furthermore, we offer a definition for the intrinsic convexity boundary and demonstrate that it's either empty or exhibits the properties of a complete, Hausdorff geodesic metric space. The space of flat cylinders is used to generate several metric spaces that are geodesically complete but fail to be intrinsic convexity CAT(0). Specifically, we explore the case where the boundary has a non-empty intersection with the ambient space and show that the completion of such an environment results in a geodesically complete but non-convex CAT(0) space. This work also relates to the study of intrinsic convexity in the context of the intrinsic geodesic completion, which was the focus of our Ph.D. research.

This research introduces a novel approach to assessing a Bayesian translator's reliability, building upon existing work on combining translation outputs from multiple models. Unlike previous works, which often relied on translation quality assessments for evaluating individual models, our method uniquely leverages actual human translations to evaluate a translator's reliability. By employing a Bayesian framework, our technique estimates a translator's dependability with greater statistical efficiency, utilizing more accurate human translations as evidence. Furthermore, our method allows for continuous evaluation of a translator's reliability using actual translations and new assessment examples, tracking the evolution of a translator's performance over time. To validate our approach, we conducted experiments on translating sentences within a corpus using a variety of popular translation systems. The results demonstrate that our method can accurately estimate a translator's reliability using relatively small sets of example translations, typically 10 to 20, while also showing that even non-Bayesian translators can exhibit increasingly reliable translations as more examples are available.

In theoretical frameworks, specific sum rules for considering all final states are derived. These sum rules for energy absorption have been established within various contexts, including time reversal invariance in nuclear reactions, light scattering in materials and in the examination of relationships between absorption coefficients and indices of refraction. We explore and illustrate the general applicability of these sum rules.

Deep neural networks, specifically the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture, have been proven effective for image classification tasks, capable of filtering out irrelevant data and retaining only essential information. Comparing fully connected neural networks to CNNs, our study aims to investigate their performance differences by directly comparing their performance. Using image recognition tasks, we observed that CNNs outperform fully connected neural networks, even when the fully connected model uses more parameters, suggesting that CNN architecture is more efficient. Our results indicate that fully connected neural networks struggle to replicate CNN's performance, suggesting that CNNs' success is not solely due to their architecture but also due to the ability to filter out irrelevant data effectively.

In many countries, particularly in the US, states use lotteries to raise revenue.
To give an example, purchasing a Powerball ticket costs $2.
Lottery players choose 5 numbers out of a pool of 45 and a powerball number out of 20.
A jackpot win occurs when both the 5 numbers and the powerball are selected correctly,
while second and third prize wins are associated with singular and dual number matches respectively.
To give  an illustration, a $2 ticket has the possibility of winning $10 for a match of one number
and a jackpot win can yield $30,000, according to data from the state of New Hampshire.
To gain insight, we apply concepts from decision theory to analyze the decision-making process of a rational buyer purchasing a lottery ticket.
To make a decision, a buyer must assess the anticipated value of the lottery ticket,
which depends on their level of risk aversion and the number of participants,
with risk aversion and the number of participants being unknown variables,
which leads to an approach of decision-making under incomplete information.
To make a decision, the buyer combines their subjective view of the risk aversion and number of participants,
which results in a combined value used to assess the anticipated value and decide whether to purchase the ticket.

A multidimensional and continuous field theory known as φ^4 is being studied, where a specific variant, denoted as φ ^Q with Q being an integer of odd parity ≥3, is explored within an O(N) symmetric framework. Research has been conducted to calculate a dimension associated with a local operator formed by Q spins with a one-loop accuracy level. Specifically, an analytical determination of this operator's anomalous dimension has been achieved, where this dimension is a parameter-dependent value based on the number of spins involved. Furthermore, research has also determined all's interaction matrix and vertex. Specifically, a six-loop calculation of this matrix and vertex has been successfully completed. Moreover, a proof has been provided that a six-loop calculation version can be derived from five-loop calculations by substituting a specific constant, γ_Q, in place of Q. This proof has been successfully implemented for all local operators with a spin count. Research has successfully completed a six-loop calculation of a vertex factor, where a specific variant, denoted as φ ^4, has been explored. Specifically, a proof has been provided that the six-loop factor can be derived from five-loop calculations by substituting a specific constant, 1/N in place of Q. This proof has been successfully implemented for a specific loop calculation.

In this research, the authors introduce a groundbreaking computational framework to investigate the interaction between electrons and phonons using a tight-binding model, expanding its scope to include three types of interactions: central, on-site energy, and nearest neighbor coupling. The efficacy of proposed models is demonstrated through comparison with experimental data on graphene's valley Hall effect and the electron-photon interaction in transition metal dichalcogenides monolayers. The researchers further explore the potential applications of these innovative interaction mechanisms in valleytronics and phononics and assess their implications for electron scattering and valley Hall conductivity.

The Neural Track, a track within the Neural Information Systems Process Conference, offers an award competition for visual domain adaptation, with the top performers being the award recipients.
